root_cause: The header JavaScript incorrectly sets aria-hidden=true on the navigation menu when the menu is not in the open state, causing assistive technology to ignore the navigation links even though they are visually visible on desktop.
repair_strategy: Remove the aria-hidden attribute modification from the syncState method, allowing the navigation to remain accessible regardless of the menu button state, while preserving aria-expanded on the button for mobile menu toggling.
expected_accessibility_effect: Navigation links will be exposed in the accessibility tree as links, allowing keyboard and screen‑reader users to reach them via Tab.
functional_risks: Removing aria-hidden may cause the menu to be announced twice if both the button and links are read, but this is acceptable and does not affect functionality.
verification_requirements: Verify that the ax name/Apply role link assertion passes after the fix.
Confirm that the menu button still toggles the navigation visibility on narrow widths (mobile breakpoint).
Ensure no visual regression: the navigation remains visible on desktop and hidden when collapsed on mobile.
